contributions.statement: If an orchestrator agent is supposed to delegate, give it read-only tools; with full tools the lead agent monopolised execution until its budget ran out and never used teammates' work.
contributions.evidence: Table 3 (36 tasks, Clopper-Pearson CIs): reference team adherence 47.2% [30.4, 64.5] vs read-only Adopter 94.4%; Fig. 3 traces show monopolisation; adherence is a participation measure (audit), single runs.

contributions.statement: Log whether a declared multi-agent workflow actually happened before crediting it; under the open role card the team's gain came from tasks where it did not collaborate, while adherent tasks scored lower.
contributions.evidence: §4.3/App. A: ITT +5.6 arises on 19 non-adherent tasks (+15.8) while 17 adherent tasks show -5.9 (sign not established).

contributions.statement: Do not credit a two-solver multi-agent design without a best-of-two single-agent baseline at equal tokens; the Duo gain here is parallel sampling plus selection.
contributions.evidence: Table 2/9: Duo +14.2 on DeepSWE at ~2.2x tokens; base harness itself below mini-swe-agent on DeepSWE (audit); no pass@2 baseline.

reason: The SOTA claim does not survive, but the measured declared-vs-realised collaboration gap and the read-only-orchestrator lever are actionable for teams wiring orchestrator/worker agents.
